title: ABFlow: Alert Bursting Flow Query in Streaming Temporal Flow Networks

statements.text: 1 (Temporal Flow Network (TFN)). A temporal flow network, denoted by G = (V, E, C, T ), is a directed graph where: (a) V is the set of nodes; T is the set of timestamps; (b) E ⊆ V × V × T is the set of temporal edges; and (c) C : V × V × T → R ≥0 is a capacity function satisfying that for all 𝑢, 𝑣 ∈ V and 𝜏 ∈ T , C(𝑢, 𝑣, 𝜏) > 0 if (𝑢, 𝑣, 𝜏) ∈ E; otherwise, C(𝑢, 𝑣, 𝜏) = 0.

To further optimize such a flow computation, we propose the strict residual network (SRN) constraints such that a maximum flow is a suffix flow if and only if these constraints are satisfied. Then, we propose a reduced-complexity solution by adjusting a maximum flow to one that satisfies the SRN constraints that enables us to apply the solution recursively. 6.1 Strict Residual Network Constraints Assume that 𝑓 is a suffix flow from a source sequence 𝑆. According to Definition 5.3, the total flow-out of sources in each suffix [𝑠𝑖 , . . . , 𝑠 |𝑆 | ] (1 ≤ 𝑖 ≤ |𝑆 |) of 𝑆 w.r.t. 𝑓 , is maximized. A maximum flow 𝑓 from 𝑆 to 𝑇 in 𝐺 is a suffix flow if and only if it satisfies the SRN constraints. 6.2 Recursive Solution (SuffixFlowrec ) In this subsection, we propose a recursive solution. When a maximum flow is found and it is not a suffix flow, we adjust it to ensure it satisfies SRN constraints and hence, it is a suffix flow (Lemma 6.2), which enables the recursive solution. Observation. Consider a residual network R (𝐺, 𝑓 ) w.r.t. a flow 𝑓 ∈ 𝐹 (𝐺, 𝑆,𝑇 ). If the flows on all augmenting paths from 𝑆𝑟 = [𝑠𝑖+1, . . . , 𝑠 |𝑆 | ] to 𝑆𝑙 = [𝑠 1, . . . , 𝑠𝑖 ] are pushed to 𝑆𝑙 , those paths are removed from R (𝐺, 𝑓 ), denoted as R (𝐺, 𝑓 ) ′ . There exists a cut (e.g., the cut shown by the red line in Fig. 8(h)) that partitions R (𝐺, 𝑓 ) ′ into subgraphs 𝐺𝑙 and 𝐺𝑟 , such that i) 𝑆𝑙 ⊆ 𝑉𝐺𝑙 , 𝑆𝑟 ⊆ 𝑉𝐺𝑟 ; and ii) no edges exist from 𝐺𝑟 to 𝐺𝑙 . This cut, denoted by (𝐺𝑙 , 𝐺𝑟 ), naturally divides the suffix flow problem into two independent subproblems. Hence, we propose the operation of contradictory augmenting path removal to generate such cuts, which is the core of the recursive solution. Contradictory Augmenting Path Removal. Consider a residual network R (𝐺, 𝑓 ) w.r.t. a flow 𝑓 ∈ 𝐹 (𝐺, 𝑆,𝑇 ), where there exists augmenting paths such that 𝑓 cannot satisfy the SRN constraints. Then, the operation of contradictory augmenting path removal for 𝑓 on R (𝐺, 𝑓 ) is to add the flow on all these augmenting paths to 𝑓 , and the residual network then does not have those paths anymore.
